create.name: Mahip Rathore
create.bio:
Mahip Rathore grew up in Ujjain in central India and practised as a lawyer before retraining in psychology; he holds a PhD in Counselling Psychology and now lives in the United States, working from Amherst, Massachusetts, and Santa Barbara, California. His meditation training comes from Vipassana retreats and from studying Advaita Vedanta with Jim Gilman, a student of Swami Chinmayananda.

His teaching treats mindfulness less as a relaxation tool and more as a way of looking directly at who is aware, moving between the Buddhist idea of no-self and the Vedantic understanding of the Self as pure awareness. He leads a free monthly meditation group and ran a recorded inquiry series called Mindfully Inquiring Non-duality, in which short sits are followed by open dialogue about direct experience. Individually he offers ninety-minute mindfulness sessions and an eight-to-ten-week relationship programme pairing daily sitting with reflective listening practised alongside a partner or small group. Alongside this teaching he works as a psychotherapist, which is not covered here. Many of his guided meditations and talks, some in Hindi, are free on his website and YouTube channel.

courses.title: Mindfulness Alignment Session
courses.description: A private ninety-minute session looking at your meditation practice, its obstacles and its strengths, drawing on both Western psychology and Eastern contemplative teaching about awareness.

courses.title: Mindful Relationship Coaching Program
courses.description: An eight-to-ten-week programme built on two practices: daily mindfulness of breath and body, and reflective listening done regularly with a partner, friend or small group.
